title: Carton supply negotiation with Vellora Packaging

segments.speaker: Neha Agarwal
segments.text: Thanks for coming in, Thomas, Divya. Let's get to the box pricing straight away.

segments.speaker: Thomas Mathew
segments.text: Of course. We sent the quote last week, 21 rupees a box for the five-ply cartons.

segments.speaker: Neha Agarwal
segments.text: That's what I want to talk about. It's two rupees more than what we paid in spring.

segments.speaker: Thomas Mathew
segments.text: Kraft paper went up almost fifteen percent since then. We're not making much at 21.

segments.speaker: Imran Shaikh
segments.text: From the warehouse side, our volume is steady, about twelve thousand boxes a month.

segments.speaker: Neha Agarwal
segments.text: Exactly. With that volume we expect better than list price.

segments.speaker: Divya Krishnan
segments.text: Twelve thousand is good volume, I agree. Our line runs your size twice a week.

segments.speaker: Thomas Mathew
segments.text: We could do 19.50 if you commit to the full twelve thousand every month.

segments.speaker: Neha Agarwal
segments.text: We can commit to the volume. But 19.50 is still high for us.

segments.speaker: Imran Shaikh
segments.text: And honestly, the last two batches had some crushed corners. That costs us too.

segments.speaker: Divya Krishnan
segments.text: That was the humid week in August. We changed the stacking in our godown after that.

segments.speaker: Imran Shaikh
segments.text: Since then it's been fine, I'll admit that.

segments.speaker: Neha Agarwal
segments.text: Let me make it simple. 18 rupees a box, twelve thousand a month, and we sign today.

segments.speaker: Thomas Mathew
segments.text: 18 is very tight. Divya, can production live with that?

segments.speaker: Divya Krishnan
segments.text: If the size stays fixed and we don't change the print, yes, 18 works.

segments.speaker: Thomas Mathew
segments.text: Okay. 18 rupees a box at twelve thousand a month. We have a deal on price.

segments.speaker: Neha Agarwal
segments.text: Good. Now payment terms. We pay at 60 days today.

segments.speaker: Thomas Mathew
segments.text: At 18 we really need 30 days. Our paper supplier wants cash.

segments.speaker: Neha Agarwal
segments.text: 30 is impossible for our finance team. Their cycle is monthly.

segments.speaker: Imran Shaikh
segments.text: What about meeting in the middle?

segments.speaker: Thomas Mathew
segments.text: 45 days, and you don't delay beyond that. That's my last offer.

segments.speaker: Neha Agarwal
segments.text: Fine. Payment terms are 45 days from the invoice date.

segments.speaker: Thomas Mathew
segments.text: Thank you. I'll put all of this into a revised quote.

segments.speaker: Neha Agarwal
segments.text: When can I have it? I need to take it to our finance head.

segments.speaker: Thomas Mathew
segments.text: Let me get it signed off internally. I'll send the revised quote next Tuesday.

segments.speaker: Neha Agarwal
segments.text: Next Tuesday is fine.

segments.speaker: Thomas Mathew
segments.text: While we're here, would you consider a two-year contract? We could hold the price longer.

segments.speaker: Neha Agarwal
segments.text: I'm not committing to two years today. Paper prices are too uncertain.

segments.speaker: Imran Shaikh
segments.text: Agreed, let's look at it again in spring if things settle.

segments.speaker: Thomas Mathew
segments.text: Understood, we'll leave the two-year idea for now.

segments.speaker: Imran Shaikh
segments.text: Another topic. We want to try the stronger seven-ply boxes for the glass products.

segments.speaker: Divya Krishnan
segments.text: We can make samples. I need your exact dimensions and the weight per box.

segments.speaker: Imran Shaikh
segments.text: I'll send them over email today, it's three sizes.

segments.speaker: Divya Krishnan
segments.text: Then I'll ship fifty samples of each size in two weeks.

segments.speaker: Neha Agarwal
segments.text: Two weeks is okay. Will that be affected by your holidays?

segments.speaker: Divya Krishnan
segments.text: Our factory shutdown for Diwali starts 7 November, but samples go before that.

segments.speaker: Imran Shaikh
segments.text: Good. Once they come, someone on our side has to run the drop test on the samples.

segments.speaker: Neha Agarwal
segments.text: Quality will have to pick that up. I'll check who's free there.

segments.speaker: Imran Shaikh
segments.text: Last time the drop test took a full day, so plan for that.

segments.speaker: Thomas Mathew
segments.text: Do you still need the boxes delivered to both docks?

segments.speaker: Imran Shaikh
segments.text: Only dock two from next month. Dock one is being repaired.

segments.speaker: Divya Krishnan
segments.text: Noted. I'll tell our transport people.

segments.speaker: Neha Agarwal
segments.text: What about the printed logo? Marketing changed the colour slightly.

segments.speaker: Thomas Mathew
segments.text: If it's a new plate, there's a one-time charge of eight thousand.

segments.speaker: Neha Agarwal
segments.text: Let me check whether the change is even needed for boxes. Hold that for now.

segments.speaker: Divya Krishnan
segments.text: No problem, we'll keep printing the current design until you tell us.

segments.speaker: Imran Shaikh
segments.text: One more thing, the pallets. Can you take the empty ones back?

segments.speaker: Thomas Mathew
segments.text: Yes, our truck can collect them on each delivery.

segments.speaker: Imran Shaikh
segments.text: That clears a lot of space for us.

segments.speaker: Neha Agarwal
segments.text: Okay, I think we've covered everything. Price, terms, quote, samples.

segments.speaker: Thomas Mathew
segments.text: Thanks Neha, it was a tough one, but fair.

segments.speaker: Neha Agarwal
segments.text: Thank you both. Safe drive back.

decisions.fact: Five-ply cartons are priced at 18 rupees each for a 12,000 per month commitment.
Payment terms are 45 days from invoice.

action_items.fact: Thomas sends the revised quote with the agreed price and terms.
Divya ships 50 samples of each seven-ply box size.
A drop test is run on the samples by the buyer's quality team; nobody named.

distractors.fact: A two-year contract was proposed and not agreed.
7 November is the vendor's Diwali shutdown, not the sample date.
